trans-unit.note: The name of the game. Never translated and never reordered. The community commonly shortens it to "Juno" or "JNO" and both are fine to keep as-is; do not invent a shortening in your own language.
The community abbreviation of "Juno: New Origins". Keep the three Latin letters unchanged.
The in-game visual programming language players use to script craft. A product name, not a word: keep it as "Vizzy" in every language.

The expression language used for custom part and control inputs, also reached from the fUnK block in Vizzy. A product name: keep as "FunkyTrees", and keep the fUnK block's spelling exactly as written.

The game's characters - the crew a player flies. A proper name: do not replace it with "astronaut", "dude", or any similar word, however tempting. Transliterating it into your language's script is fine, as long as you do it consistently.
The studio that makes the game. Never translated.

Personal and organisation names in the credits are never translated or transliterated. Where a credit reads "by <name>", translate only the word "by" and leave the name exactly as written. This applies to every name in the credits screen.
The star at the centre of the main system. The game is named after it.
The home planet, where players launch from. Wordplay on the studio name, Jundroo.
A moon of Droo. Named after Brigantium, the Roman name for the city of A Coruna.
A moon of Droo, sharing the Latin name of our own Moon.
A moon of Droo. Keep the letters and both periods exactly as written.
A planet, tidally locked to Juno and the hottest world in the system. Named after Vulcan, the Roman god of fire.
A planet, volcanic, with lava lakes and obsidian terrain. The name was coined by the community, referencing sergals.
A moon of Sergeaa. The name is "Droo" spelled backwards. If your language transliterates Droo, mirror that here so the reversal still reads - this relationship matters more than the letters.
A planet, the game's Mars analogue. The name was picked for its sound and carries no meaning.
A moon of Cylero. Named after Niobe of Greek mythology.
A moon of Cylero. Named after the herma, a Greek sculpture associated with Hermes.
A comet. The name is wordplay on Halley's Comet and Andrew, the creator of the game.
A planet. The name was proposed by the community. It shares the "-dos" ending with Urados on purpose; keep the two matching in your language.
A moon of Tydos. "Nebra" is the Galician word for fog.
A moon of Tydos. Inherited from a community project, where the name referenced the moon Miranda; it was later reworked to resemble Iapetus.
A moon of Tydos. Named after Orcus of Roman mythology.
A planet. The name blends Uranus with the "-dos" ending of Tydos; the two planets are meant to share that ending, so keep them matching in your language.
A moon of Urados. The name blends Jastro, a well-known member of the community, with Janus.
A moon of Urados. Named after Boreas of Greek mythology.
A moon of Urados. The name was proposed by the community.
A moon of Urados. The name blends Hypatch, a well-known member of the community, with Hyperion.
A celestial body. "Cladh" is Scottish Gaelic for graveyard.
Anything the player builds and flies - rocket, plane, rover, probe or station. The general word; prefer it over 'vehicle' or 'ship' unless the English says otherwise.
A single component placed in the Designer (a tank, wing, engine). The building block of a craft.
A group of parts activated together, and the act of separating them. Both noun and verb appear in the UI.
The ordered list of stages, and the system that fires them in sequence.
A numbered group of parts toggled together by the player. Always paired with a number in the UI.

The part that gives a craft control. Deliberately broad: it may be a crewed space capsule, a bare probe chip, or an open seat with a Drood sitting in it. Do not narrow it to 'capsule' or 'cockpit' - a craft without one cannot be steered, and that is the point of the term.
A saved cluster of parts reused across craft. One word in this game, not 'sub-assembly'.
The build-mode scene where craft are assembled. Capitalised when naming the scene.
The career-mode progression screen where parts and features are unlocked.
The career-mode currency spent to unlock nodes in the Tech Tree, earned by flying and completing objectives. Abbreviated TP directly after the number, as in '250TP'. Keep the abbreviation.
A game mode: everything unlocked, no funds, no objectives. A mode name.
A game mode: contracts, funds, and parts unlocked through the Tech Tree. A mode name.

A game mode, sitting between Sandbox and Career: it starts with all parts unlocked, a large amount of money, and cheats available, while keeping career features. A mode name. Do not confuse it with 'Hybrid Jets', which is an engine type and unrelated.
A career-mode job offering a reward for completing objectives.

In career mode this is a precise term, not a general one: the specific part a contract requires a craft to carry to its objective. The UI warns when it is missing from the craft, so translate it as a definite, identifiable part rather than as 'cargo' in general.
The navigation ball showing the craft's orientation and manoeuvre directions.
The engine power control, as noun and verb.
The force an engine produces.
Aerodynamic resistance opposing motion through an atmosphere.
The aerodynamic force a wing generates perpendicular to airflow.
The total velocity change a craft can produce. Keep the hyphen and both capitals; it is a standard aerospace term, not a coined one.
Specific impulse - a measure of engine efficiency. An abbreviation; keep it as 'Isp' unless your language has an established equivalent.
Reaction Control System - the small thrusters used for fine attitude control. Keep the abbreviation.
The path of a craft around a celestial body, as noun and verb.
The highest point of an orbit. Standard orbital mechanics term - use your language's established astronomical word if it has one.
The lowest point of an orbit. Standard orbital mechanics term.
The tilt of an orbit relative to the body's equator, in degrees. Standard orbital mechanics term.
How far an orbit departs from a circle: 0 is circular, approaching 1 is a long ellipse. Standard orbital mechanics term.
Half the long axis of an elliptical orbit - the standard measure of its size.
The point where an orbit crosses the reference plane going north. Standard orbital mechanics term.
The craft's angular position along its orbit, measured from periapsis. Standard orbital mechanics term.
The region where a celestial body's gravity dominates. Often abbreviated SOI in English text.
Any planet, moon, star, comet or asteroid. The neutral umbrella term.
The gas layer around a body, which produces drag and allows air-breathing engines.
Returning through an atmosphere at high speed, generating heat.
A part storing propellant.
The consumable an engine burns. Prefer the specific fuel name where the English uses one.

A place a craft can be launched from - the built-in sites and any spot the player saves for reuse. Each has size and weight limits a craft must fit within, so it is a specific named location, not scenery.
The Droods aboard a craft. Collective noun.
The career-mode currency used to buy parts and launch craft, distinct from Tech Points. Plural in English.
